about.title: Point Arena Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Point Arena is a small coastal community of roughly 446 people, but the businesses, motels, and public spaces along Port Road, Main Street, and Lake Street still carry the same legal responsibilities as anywhere else in California. Property owners and managers have a duty to keep walkways, stairs, and floors reasonably safe, and to fix or warn about known hazards. When a wet floor, broken step, uneven pavement, or poor lighting causes a fall, the property owner may be liable — but only if it can be shown they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the danger. Because Point Arena is rural and many properties don't have dedicated security staff, gathering evidence quickly matters even more here. Photos of the hazard, witness names, and any surveillance footage from a nearby shop or motel can make a real difference. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself, but we can put you in touch with an independent attorney who works on a contingency basis to review what happened and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in Point Arena

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner had actual or constructive notice of the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaint records, and witness statements to establish that notice.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Video Before It's Erased
items.desc: Many small businesses and motels overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of any video can be critical to supporting your claim.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning your recovery can be reduced but not eliminated if you were partly at fault. An independent attorney can help explain how this might apply to your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Point Arena?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government-owned property or public sidewalk in Mendocino County is involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim filing. Because these deadlines are strict, it's wise to speak with an attorney as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell at a business on Main Street or near Port Road and no one saw it happen?
items.answer: Even without witnesses, evidence like photos of the hazard, your clothing or shoes, and any nearby surveillance cameras can help support your claim. Many Point Arena businesses are small, so footage may only be kept briefly, making prompt documentation important. An attorney can help identify what evidence to gather and preserve.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we don't charge you anything to find an independent attorney for your case. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
